newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end up following JGBs' rise.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end up following JGBs' rise.

text.p: Key September Euroyen futures ended Thursday's TIFFE day session slightly higher following a rise in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
The September closed up 0.01 at 99.30, after trading between 99.31 and 99.27. Volume was 33,709 contracts.
The key March JGB futures contract ended up 0.35 at 126.08.
The failure of Tokyo stocks to extend earlier gains also helped support Euroyen futures, traders said.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended up 51.21 points, or 0.28 percent, at 18,144.34, after rising as high as 18,317.63 in the morning.
A weak stock market is considered supportive for Euroyen futures as it underscores the need for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to maintain a low-interest rate policy.
"Euroyen futures rose as JGB futures ended near its intra-day high and stocks erased much of their earlier gains," said a city bank trader.
Market participants were also relieved by a relatively stable yen, traders said.
The dollar was stuck between 116.65 and 116.97 yen in Tokyo, after rising to around 117.48 yen overnight.
Machinery orders data for November released in the afternoon had limited impact on Euroyen futures, traders said.

Japan's November private-sector machinery orders, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, fell 9.7 percent month-on-month. A decline had been widely expected after a hefty 44.2 percent increase in orders for October.
Market participants may shift their interest to December futures as the September is starting to look heavy near 99.35, a trader at a trust bank said.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.49 percent, up from Tuesday's weighted average of 0.48 percent.
Japan's financial markets were closed on Wednesday for a national holiday.
The BOJ injected a net 400 billion yen into the money market on Thursday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
About 20 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.53 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.
